5.8: 5.8 But after. And the children of Israel, circumcised, rested in the same place, sitting in the camp, until they were healed. It is not enough to be circumcised; it is necessary after circumcision to be healed, and for the scar to form over the wound. To be circumcised through Jesus, then, is to lay aside vices and wicked habits and the worst practices, and to cut off whatever is at variance with the rule of honesty. But in doing this we are bound by a certain difficulty, since with a certain grief of mind we avoid the fault of custom by a newly formed practice: at this time, therefore, we are said, as in the pain of our circumcision, to sit still, until the scar has formed and we are healed, that is, until we fulfill the new practices without difficulty, and what at first seemed unaccustomed and hard is turned into habit; and then it is rightly said to us: This day I have taken away the reproach of Egypt from you. And they kept. After the reproach of Egypt was taken away, the children of Israel kept the Passover on the fourteenth day of the month. For neither before circumcision, nor after it, before they were healed, could they eat the flesh of the lamb: you see, then, that no unclean person keeps the Passover, no uncircumcised. Note the order: after we cross, with Jesus Christ as leader, through the streams of the washing, and by faith are marked with spiritual circumcision, then at last we celebrate the Passover, that is, we believe Christ sacrificed for the salvation of the world, and believing, are at once fed with the bread of the Lord's body.

Each one of us ought to fulfill these things in himself. You have in yourself Jesus as leader through faith. Make for yourself trumpets of beaten work from the holy Scriptures, draw from them your thoughts, from them your words; for that is why they are called trumpets of beaten work. Sound them, that is, in psalms, in hymns, in spiritual songs. If you have sounded on such trumpets, and carried the ark of the testament around seven times, that is, if you do not separate the mystical precepts of the law from the evangelical trumpets, so too may you demand of yourself the consent of jubilation, that is, if the people of your thoughts and senses always bring forth a concordant and harmonious voice; and if you do not sometimes speak truth and sometimes lie by flattering, if you are not at one time pleasant in forgiveness, at another savage in anger; and if within you the flesh does not lust against the spirit and the spirit against the flesh, send forth the voice of jubilation, because the world has been conquered for you. Hence Paul said: But far be it from me to glory, except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom the world is crucified to me, and I to the world Gal. 5. The walls at once. Hence Paul: He took away what was against us, nailing it to the cross, and despoiling principalities and powers, he led them away openly, triumphing over them on the wood of the cross Col. 2. From these words I understand that the heavenly powers, principalities and powers, seeing the battle of Jesus, the strong man bound and his vessels plundered, blew the heavenly trumpets, because, the prince of the world bound, the world was conquered, and the heavenly host gave the voice of jubilation in the triumph of Christ Matt. 12. Truly, then, the people of the Gentiles is set free who knows this jubilation and recognizes and believes the mysteries.

15.1: 15.1 Now the lot of the children of Judah, etc. Although it is the custom of Holy Scripture to name the four parts of the world, which they call axes or regions, in the description of the borders of the tribe of Judah only two are named. And the borders, he says, of the children of the tribe of Judah according to their peoples were made from the borders of Edom, from the desert of Zin to the west. And when he had described the borders from the west, he says, and on the east the Salt Sea, but passed over the north and south in silence. The borders of Judah, then, are next to the borders of Edom, which is interpreted earthly: for after earthly things the borders of Judah follow at once, but from the desert, he says, of Zin, that is, of temptations. After temptations, then, the borders of the inheritance of Judah follow. East and West are named for neighboring places, which we said above, that is, confines. The valley of Egypt is also designated as neighboring the western parts, which is from the desert to the west. On the east the borders are girded by the Salt Sea. After this, he says, from the hills which stretch toward the west, and from there one goes up from the west as far as Kadesh-barnea, and so it extends from west to Kadesh. These are their borders from Africa, and from there it went on to the valley of Egypt. See how in the western parts he names Africa, Egypt and the sunset, that each may know these are to be passed through, and so at last come to the royal tribe, from which our Lord arose. From the borders of Edom is the desert of Zin; so we must cross the wilderness of temptations, that we may come into the inheritance of the children of Judah. We must also climb the ascent of the hills of Akrabbim, which is interpreted scorpions, because the scorpions must be passed over and trodden down by us, of which it is written: Behold, I have given you power to tread upon serpents and scorpions, etc. Luke 10. Whoever wishes to enter the inheritance of the tribe of Judah, let him climb these ascents, tread on and escape these scorpions. Perhaps the Lord was saying this to Ezekiel making this journey: Son of man, you dwell in the midst of scorpions Ezek. 2. And the borders, he says, are as far as Kadesh-barnea. Kadesh is interpreted holy or sanctification. The borders of Judah therefore reach to sanctification. It is also said that on the east of Judah is the Salt Sea, and afterward in his part is named the fountain of the sun, and the city of the sun, and in the same tribe is also the city of letters. Everyone, therefore, who wishes to enter into the portion of the children of Judah must first cross the Salt Sea, that is, overcome the waves and whirlwinds of this world, and escape all that is in this world, which for its uncertainty and slipperiness is compared to sea waves, that he may be able to come to the land of Judah, and to the fountain of the sun of justice, which is a fountain of water springing up unto life eternal, and afterward find the city of the sun of justice. There is also in Egypt a city of the sun, but that took the name of this sun which the heavenly Father commands to rise upon the good and the evil Matt. 5. But that which is in Judea is made only of saints, because it is the city of God, and that fountain mentioned above, become a river, makes glad the city of God Ps. 45. You too, if you are fortified on every side, and surrounded by the wall of continence, strengthened by the towers of patience and magnanimity, will be made a city of God. But if to this you add the light of the knowledge of God, and the sun of justice shines upon you, you will be made a city of the sun, or you will inherit by lot the city of the sun. If you study the law of God day and night, and the book of the law does not depart from your hand, your inheritance will be made the city of letters. ADAMANTIUS, Homily 20 on Joshua.
